title: Likes and Dislikes
sourceNote: The transcript is very garbled. Some of the teacher's sentences (especially the ones with past tense and some adverbs) were reconstructed into standard German.
objectives: I can say that I like something with *gefallen*
I can say that I do not like something
I can strengthen my opinion with adverbs (sehr, ganz, echt, gar nicht)
I can ask someone's opinion with *Wie findest du ...?*

vocab.en: to please, to be liked by

expressions.en: I think that is really great.

expressions.de: Das gefällt mir nicht so gut.
expressions.en: I don't like that so much.
I don't like that at all.
What do you think of that?

patterns.en: I think the book is great.
What do you think of the hat?

grammar.title: Saying you like something: gefallen
grammar.body:
In German you do not say 'I like it' but literally 'It pleases me': **Das gefällt mir.** The thing you like is the subject; the person who likes it is in the dative (**mir, dir**). In **Das gefällt mir** the word **das** can be replaced by a person or a thing: **Er gefällt mir.** (e.g. *der Hut*), **Sie gefällt mir.** (e.g. *die Hose*), **Es gefällt mir.** (e.g. *das Kleid*).

To ask: **Gefällt dir das?**
grammar.ar: الشيء المُعجِب هو الفاعل، والشخص بصيغة المفعول غير المباشر: mir (لي)، dir (لك).

examples.en: Yes, I like it very much.

grammar.title: Plural: gefallen
grammar.body: When the thing you like is plural, the verb is **gefallen** (not *gefällt*).

examples.en: I don't like them at all.

grammar.title: Dative pronouns
grammar.body: After **gefallen** you need the dative form of the person.

grammar.title: Strengthening with adverbs
grammar.body:
Add an adverb to make your feeling stronger: **sehr**, **ganz**, **echt**. Do not mix positive adverbs with negative ones.

For dislikes use **nicht**, **nicht so gut** or **gar nicht**. You can also say what you think with **finden**: **Das finde ich toll / schlecht.**

examples.en: I don't like that at all.

grammar.title: Talking about something that happened
grammar.body: To give an opinion about something that already took place, use **war**: **Es war super.** **Es war toll.** **Es war klasse.**

mistakes.why: The thing is the subject; the person is dative (*mir*).
Plural subject needs the plural verb.

pronunciation.tip: After *e*, *i*, *ä*: a soft hissing sound, like a cat: *schlecht*, *echt*, *nicht*.

lines.de: Hallo Tom! Wie findest du mein Kleid?
lines.en: Hi Tom! What do you think of my dress?

lines.de: Es gefällt mir sehr. Es ist ganz toll!
lines.en: I like it a lot. It's really great!

lines.de: Danke! Und wie findest du die Schuhe?
lines.en: Thanks! And what do you think of the shoes?

lines.de: Die Schuhe gefallen mir nicht so gut.
lines.en: I don't like the shoes so much.

tip: Learn *Das gefällt mir* as one block, and remember that *mir* and *dir* stay the same for every noun.

comprehension.q: How do you say 'I like that'?
How do you say 'I don't like that at all'?
Which verb do you use for plural things: gefällt or gefallen?

items.q: Gefällt ___ das Buch? (Do you like it?)
Der Hut gefällt ___ gar nicht. (I don't like it)
Wie gefällt ___ das Auto? (How do you like it?)

exercises.title: Like or dislike?
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct ending for the meaning in brackets.

items.q: Das gefällt mir ___. (sehr / gar nicht) - I like it very much.
Das gefällt mir ___. (sehr / gar nicht) - I don't like it at all.
Ich finde das ___. (toll / schlecht) - I think it's great.
Ich finde das ___. (klasse / schlecht) - I think it's bad.

exercises.title: Word order
exercises.instructions: Put the words in the correct order.

items.q: What do you think of the dress?

items.a: Es war toll. / Es war super. / Es war klasse.

summary: Likes: **Das gefällt mir.** / **Gefällt dir das?** - the person is dative (**mir, dir**).
Dislikes: **Das gefällt mir nicht.** / **nicht so gut** / **gar nicht.**
Opinions with **finden**: **Ich finde das toll / super / klasse / schlecht.** Past: **Es war toll.**
Strengthen with **sehr, ganz, echt**; plural things: **Die Schuhe gefallen mir.**
